One translator initially fell (2) ____ on rhyming phrases whenever a literal version sounded awkward. The results were fluent, yet some introduced cheerful images into an otherwise bleak poem. Such additions (3) ____ its tone rather than merely changing its wording. The editor therefore asked her to explain the (4) ____ behind each departure from the original.

The team eventually reached a (5) ____: the spoken translation would retain more detail, while the captions would use shorter sentences. The organisers explicitly wanted the versions to complement each other, not for either to (6) ____ the other. Both would be available together. The editor rejected an explanation of the poet's entire career as beyond the (7) ____ of these brief captions. Instead, she required a note identifying where compression had removed a meaningful ambiguity. That would make the limitations (8) ____ to readers rather than leave them concealed.

completed_passage:
A literary festival (0) commissioned new translations of poems for a public reading. The translators also had to supply short captions. These could not do justice to every feature of the originals, but they had to preserve the central images.

One translator initially fell back on rhyming phrases whenever a literal version sounded awkward. The results were fluent, yet some introduced cheerful images into an otherwise bleak poem. Such additions distorted its tone rather than merely changing its wording. The editor therefore asked her to explain the rationale behind each departure from the original.

The team eventually reached a compromise: the spoken translation would retain more detail, while the captions would use shorter sentences. The organisers explicitly wanted the versions to complement each other, not for either to supplant the other. Both would be available together. The editor rejected an explanation of the poet's entire career as beyond the scope of these brief captions. Instead, she required a note identifying where compression had removed a meaningful ambiguity. That would make the limitations explicit to readers rather than leave them concealed.
